skill.name: binary-re-tool-setup
skill.description: Guides setup and troubleshooting for binary reverse engineering tools, including radare2, Ghidra, GDB, QEMU, Frida, and cross-compilation toolchains.
skill.summary: Set up and verify binary reverse engineering toolchains across common platforms.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate reverse engineering setup guidance, but it includes high-risk operational instructions. Confirmed risks include privileged Docker, sudo package and system changes, curl-to-shell installation, persistent startup-file edits, and unpinned third-party source installs. Most generic backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives.

remediation.issue: Privileged Docker commands are recommended for binfmt setup.
remediation.suggestion: Move binfmt registration to a manual prerequisite and require explicit user confirmation before any privileged container command.

remediation.issue: A remote installer is executed through curl and shell command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell with pinned release downloads, checksum verification, and visible installation steps.

remediation.issue: Several setup steps require sudo or administrator shells.
remediation.suggestion: Separate privileged commands from normal setup and require clear user approval for each privileged action.

remediation.issue: Shell and debugger startup files are modified persistently.
remediation.suggestion: Make startup-file edits optional, idempotent, and reversible, with exact before-and-after changes shown to the user.

remediation.issue: Third-party source installs are not pinned or verified.
remediation.suggestion: Pin repository commits or release tags and verify signatures or checksums before building or installing.

static_findings.snippet: - Copy binaries into `~` rather than using `/mnt/c/...` paths (fewer permission issues)
- Use `wsl --shutdown` in PowerShell to restart WSL after config changes
Since Homebrew doesn't provide `qemu-user`, use Docker for cross-architecture execution:
**IMPORTANT:** On Colima, always mount from `~/` not `/tmp/`:
| `pdg` unknown command | Plugin not loaded | `r2pm -ci r2ghidra` |
| Decompilation hangs | Large function | Use `pdf` instead, or Ghidra headless |
| `exec format error` in Docker | binfmt not registered | `docker run --privileged tonistiigi/binfmt
| `libXXX.so not found` | Missing dependency | `apt install` in container (check `rabin2 -l`) |
| r2 `pdg` unknown command | r2ghidra not installed | `r2pm -ci r2ghidra` |
| Empty xrefs from `axtj` | Shallow analysis | Use `aa; aac` or manual `af @addr` |
| Empty Docker mount | Colima /tmp issue | Use `~/path` instead of `/tmp/path` |
| strace fails in container | ptrace not implemented | Use `LD_DEBUG=files,libs` |
- Use `wsl --shutdown` in PowerShell to restart WSL after config changes

content.value_statement: Reverse engineering work stalls when essential tools are missing or misconfigured. This skill guides setup for radare2, Ghidra, GDB, QEMU, Frida, and related toolchains.
actual_capabilities: Lists required reverse engineering tools and their priorities.
Provides setup guidance for Ubuntu, Debian, WSL2, macOS, Docker, and Arch Linux.
Covers radare2, Ghidra, GEF, Frida, Unicorn, Angr, and YARA setup.
Explains sysroot setup for Debian, Ubuntu, device, and Alpine musl targets.
Includes a tool verification script for required and optional components.
Troubleshoots common QEMU, Docker, GDB, Ghidra, and library problems.
limitations: Several commands require administrator rights and should not run without review.
The skill does not verify installer signatures or package integrity by itself.
Package names and recommended versions can change across distributions.
It focuses on tool setup, not full binary analysis methodology.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Analysis Workstation
use_cases.description: Install and verify core tools before starting reverse engineering work on Linux, WSL2, or macOS.

use_cases.title: Repair a Broken Toolchain
use_cases.description: Diagnose missing commands, plugin failures, QEMU errors, and library path problems.

use_cases.title: Set Up Cross-Architecture Testing
use_cases.description: Configure QEMU, sysroots, and debuggers for ARM and other non-native binaries.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Toolchain
prompt_templates.prompt: Check which required binary reverse engineering tools are missing on this machine. Ask before running installation commands.

prompt_templates.title: Install Core Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a Linux binary reverse engineering environment with radare2, QEMU user mode, GDB multiarch, and binutils.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Cross-Architecture Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: My ARM binary does not run under QEMU. Check architecture, sysroot paths, loader paths, and debugger setup.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Safe Setup Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe, reviewable setup plan for Ghidra, GEF, Frida, Angr, and YARA. Separate privileged steps from normal user steps.

output_examples.input: I need ARM binary analysis tools on Ubuntu.
output: A prioritized checklist for radare2, qemu-user, gdb-multiarch, binutils, and ARM sysroots.
A clear separation between package installation, verification, and optional tooling.
Notes about commands that require administrator approval.

output_examples.input: GDB cannot run my ARM binary.
output: A diagnosis path for architecture mismatch, missing loader files, and sysroot configuration.
Suggested checks for QEMU gdbserver and gdb-multiarch connection settings.
Warnings before changing linker paths or system files.

output_examples.input: I want Ghidra and radare2 decompilation ready.
output: Setup guidance for radare2, r2ghidra, and Ghidra headless support.
Verification steps for plugin availability and headless analyzer access.
Memory and timeout notes for large binaries.

best_practices: Review every privileged command before execution.
Use pinned releases and checksums for third-party tools when possible.
Run risky dynamic analysis inside isolated containers or virtual machines.
anti_patterns: Do not execute remote installer scripts without inspecting and pinning them.
Do not run privileged Docker containers on untrusted hosts.
Do not append to shell startup files without user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill analyze binaries directly?
faq.answer: No. It helps configure tools used for binary analysis and debugging.

faq.question: Can it install tools automatically?
faq.answer: It provides installation guidance, but privileged commands should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Ubuntu, Debian, WSL2, macOS, Docker-based workflows, and Arch Linux.

faq.question: Does it support cross-architecture analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers QEMU user mode, sysroots, gdb-multiarch, and related troubleshooting.

faq.question: Is Ghidra required?
faq.answer: No. Ghidra is recommended for decompilation, while radare2 and core command-line tools are required.

faq.question: Why is the security risk high?
faq.answer: The guide includes sudo commands, privileged Docker, remote installers, and persistent startup file changes.
